name: Pro-Nominal One and Ones
pattern: Nom[one/ones as anaphoric head + optional nominal dependents]

entry.name: Pro-Nominal One and Ones
entry.pattern: Nom[one/ones as anaphoric head + optional nominal dependents]

1.definition: Recovers a nominal description while allowing independent determination and number.

projection.target: Ones can take plural morphology and an adjective. It normally recovers count nominal content, while the separate numeral one can answer a question about cardinality.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: One and ones standing in for a noun
curious.summary: The words one and ones can stand in for a noun that was already mentioned, so we don't repeat it.
curious.body:
In I preferred the larger ones, the word ones picks up a description from earlier, such as shoes or cups. It carries that description, and it can still take its own the, an adjective like larger, and a plural ending.

This dictionary says it normally stands in for something countable. The number word one is a separate thing: it can answer a question about how many. This dictionary marks the account as provisional.
curious.try: Say a sentence about some things, then refer back to them with ones and an adjective, as in the larger ones.

teacher.summary: Explains one and ones as substitute words that recover a noun and can take their own determiner, adjective and plural.
teacher.explain: Pro-nominal one(s) is an anaphoric head that recovers a nominal description while allowing independent determination and number. In I preferred the larger ones, ones can take plural morphology, a determiner (the) and an adjective (larger). It normally recovers count nominal content. The numeral one is separate and can answer a question about cardinality. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and gives one constructed example, so check further cases before generalizing.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called the 'prop-word one' or 'substitute one' in traditional grammars; this dictionary calls it pro-nominal one.
watch_for: A learner might read ones as the numeral one with a plural ending.
A learner might think ones can recover any kind of noun, when this dictionary says it normally recovers count nominal content.
teacher.activity: Students get a sentence with a repeated noun, such as one about two kinds of cups, and replace the second noun with one or ones and an adjective. They compare their versions.

child.hook: How can you talk about some things again without saying the same word twice?
child.explain: The word ones can stand in for a word we've already used. If we're talking about shoes, we can say the larger ones. It means the larger shoes.
child.play: Name a group of things, like pencils. Then say which ones you like using ones, such as the sharp ones.

checked.note: Audit: fixed curious.body, which gave a causal link (because it carries that description) that the entry does not make, and the child hook and explain, which called the noun shoes a name. Also replaced the entry with this dictionary in curious and teacher text, Often with Sometimes in teacher.terms, and restated the count limit with the entry's normally.
